course_name_original: ENGLISH FOR PROFESSIONAL AND ACADEMIC COMMUNICATION (565000332)
course_name_en: English for Professional and Academic Communication
prerequisites: Official B1 English language proficiency (CEFR) is required for enrollment.
Official B2 English language proficiency (CEFR) is required to pass the course.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate, and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them while working in multidisciplinary teams.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong study for appropriate professional development.
Organization and planning of projects and human teams. Teamwork and leadership capacity.
Use of the English language at written and oral level.
Ability to defend ideas and points of view indicating pros and cons of different options. Attitudes of critical reasoning and creative actions based on open situations.
Knowledge and capacities to understand the main ideas of complex general and specialized texts.
Ability to interact with English speakers with a sufficient degree of fluency and naturalness.
Ability to produce clear and detailed texts on diverse topics.

teaching_methods: Practice of language structures and vocabulary
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain a score of 50% or more in each assessment component, and must also accredit an official B2 English language level. For Progressive Evaluation, the final grade is calculated from a Final Exam (45%), Reading Comprehension Test (10%), Oral Presentation (15%), and continuous Skills Labs (30% from 12 activities); if a student fails to achieve 50% in the continuous Skills Labs, they must take the Skills Labs Test. For Global Evaluation (Ordinary and Extraordinary calls), the final grade is based on a Final Exam (45%), Skills Labs Test (30%), Reading Comprehension Test (10%), and Oral Presentation (15%). Failure to accredit B2 proficiency at least five working days before the exam results in a maximum grade of 4.0 in the ordinary call, and "No Presentado" in the extraordinary call.
bibliography: Ibbotson, Mark. Cambridge English for Engineering Student's Book. Cambridge University Press, 2008.
